messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content: If you ignore air resistance, the only acceleration acting on the ball after it leaves your hand is due to gravity. That acceleration is approximately \(g \approx 9.8\;\text{m/s}^2\) directed downward. In vector form, you could write it as \(\mathbf{a} = -9.8\,\hat{\mathbf{y}}\;\text{m/s}^2\), where the negative sign indicates that the acceleration points opposite to the upward direction you chose as positive.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" They want the acceleration. But acceleration due to gravity is constant ~9.8 m/s^2 downward. So answer: -9.8 m/s^2 (negative sign indicates direction). We can also mention ignoring air resistance. No need to call function.
